headline: Gravity ramp lifts revenue but losses widen sharply
summary_short: Lucid's Q1 FY2026 revenue rose 20.2% y/y to $282.5M on the Lucid Gravity ramp-up, but the net loss widened to $1,028.3M (-$3.46 diluted EPS) as inventory write-downs, tariff costs, and higher R&D/SG&A spend outweighed an estimated $53.0M IEEPA tariff refund, and stockholders' equity flipped to a $351.4M deficit.
summary_long: Revenue grew 20.2% y/y to $282.5M as Gravity's higher-ASP mix offset a $31.5M drop in regulatory-credit sales. Gross margin worsened to -110.4% (from -97.2%) on $237.9M of inventory write-downs and $41.0M of incremental tariff cost, partly offset by an estimated $53.0M IEEPA tariff refund. R&D rose 34% on Midsize-platform spend and SG&A rose 43%, plus a $37.9M workforce-reduction charge under the 2026 Plan. Net loss widened to $1,028.3M as a $274.3M smaller preferred-stock derivative gain and higher note interest outweighed operating trends. Cash, equivalents and investments fell to $714.0M; management guides FY2026 capex of $1.2-1.4B. Stockholders' equity turned to a $351.4M deficit as Series A/B preferred stock sits in mezzanine equity.

drivers.explanation: Net loss widened on continued Gravity-ramp inventory write-downs, tariff costs, higher R&D/SG&A spend and a workforce-reduction charge, plus a much smaller preferred-stock derivative fair-value gain than a year ago; partly offset by an estimated IEEPA tariff refund.
Grew 20% y/y primarily on the Lucid Gravity ramp-up, whose higher average selling price produced a favorable mix; partly offset by a $31.5M drop in regulatory-credit sales.

Cost of revenue rose 28% y/y on higher inventory write-downs (including firm-purchase-commitment losses), ~$41.0M of incremental tariff cost, and higher Gravity unit costs, partly offset by an estimated $53.0M IEEPA tariff refund.

Total operating expenses rose 46% y/y: R&D +34% on Midsize-platform engineering and headcount, SG&A +43% on stock comp, payroll and facilities costs, plus a new $37.9M workforce-reduction charge under the 2026 Plan.
Not a company-reported caption; equals pretax loss ($1,028.2M) plus interest expense ($41.1M), so it tracks the same operating deterioration plus higher note interest.
Not a company-reported caption; equals EBIT plus depreciation & amortization ($116.4M), so it tracks EBIT with a roughly flat D&A add-back.

Other income swung from +$324.4M to -$38.7M, mainly a $274.3M smaller fair-value gain on the redeemable convertible preferred stock's derivative liability and $29.2M higher interest expense from the 2030/2031 Notes.

Net loss attributable to common stockholders includes $106.0M of Series A/B preferred accretion this quarter versus $364.9M a year ago, so EPS improved less on a raw net-income basis but the y/y comparison is dampened by that shrinking accretion charge.

Declined on $1,185.7M of operating cash outflow and $253.2M of capex during the quarter; the release notes $550M of Series C preferred and a $500M DDTL draw arrived after quarter-end.
Not separately explained beyond the overall net-loss widening described in Results of Operations; the release does not itemize working-capital drivers of the cash-flow-statement change.
Rose on continued expansion of AMP-1 in Casa Grande, Arizona and construction of the CBU portion of AMP-2 in Saudi Arabia.

Turned to a deficit because Series A/B (and, after quarter-end, Series C) redeemable convertible preferred stock sits in mezzanine/temporary equity outside permanent stockholders' equity, while the quarter's ~$1.03B net loss further reduced accumulated deficit.
